title: carol joins, then alice plays, optimized

timeline.label: Carol joins the game. `len`, the length of her name, sits on the stack. `name` isn't copied anywhere. The compiler's data points straight at the name's bytes in the call data, using its offset and length, saved in memory.
The name is written to storage, into Carol's record. On the way, the code copies its bytes from the call data into memory, then stores them a word at a time.
Alice plays. The code copies her player record from storage into memory, and `player` now lives there.

The optimizer has inlined `_applyCombo`: its code runs right here, with no real call. The compiler's data still marks where the call begins, so only `_applyCombo`'s own variables are listed. `mult` has no location yet.
`mult` now has a location: 8 bytes of memory.
`mult = combo` doesn't copy anything. The compiler's data now points `mult` at `combo`'s own bytes, so the two variables share one location.
Back in `play()`. `_applyCombo`'s variables are gone, and `gained`, the result it returned, now has a location in memory.
